body_html:
A month ago, my good colleague SEO-mir (real name: Tihomir!), asked me if I knew of a tool, editors could use to write content, enriched with structured data. I didn’t, unfortunately. But I quickly made a wishlist for such a tool:

  • Should be able to run as a bookmarklet — ie. as an overlay to any existing CMS-solution.
  • Should be easy to extend with new schemas, as new schemas are constantly created and/or changed.
  • The content creator / editor should be able to select the output format (tags) for any schema property.
  • The interface designer should be able to set required fields, field order etc. for any schema.

Now, a month later, I’m able to set a check-mark for all the requirements on my original wishlist:
http://www.stoumann.dk/examples/editor/

Structured Markup Editor

There are still a lot on my to-do-list —  new ideas, such as:

  • JSON-LD export
  • TinyMCE-plugin
  • Advanced mode

— but the basic editor is there.

A content editor can pick among some of the most popular schemas:

Article
Book
Download
Event
LocalBusiness
Organization
Person
Product
Question
Recipe
Review
Video

— Fill out the selected form, click on “Generate Schema”, and follow the on-screen guide.

The bookmarklet is also in place (click the Info-link from the tool), but will only work with “http”-connections, as my own domain doesn’t support SSL.

I’m working on a solution, where the editor will be on a domain that supports both connection types.

So — go ahead — create some structured markup! Now you don’t have an excuse!

I’d very much like to hear from you if you have suggestions / feedback.
